question: why does the geometry check block 78 of 85 executed figures
answer: both of its failing rules judge individual pixels, and every offending pixel in the cohort is isolated speckle -- no figure has lost structure

skeleton_coverage_lost.rule: fail when fraction<0.80 OR p95>4.0 OR max>8.0, on per-pixel skeleton-to-model distance over ~40k pixels
skeleton_coverage_lost.interpretation: max is the extreme order statistic of a per-pixel distance over tens of thousands of samples, so a single speck exceeds any fixed bound. Lost content is connected; nothing in this cohort was lost.

stage2_residual_pending.rule: review when any source pixel is unrepresented

largest_residual_CONNECTED_run_px.note: exactly 1 on all 91 figures -- not one has two adjacent unrepresented pixels

change.raster_recall: largest_unsupported_run_pixels > 16 replaces max > 8.0; fraction and p95 rules unchanged
change.counts_retained: both checks still record residual_source_pixels and the run length, so a stray pixel stays visible in the evidence

remaining: The entire gap to a training corpus is now unknown_reference_text on 80 figures. 82 of 85 executed figures would be accepted if it were cleared.
still_of_the_same_shape: geometry_output_off_skeleton, the precision half of the raster check, still uses the raw max against 8.0 px over the same sample. It fires on 1 figure today.
